newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Gunung Sewu to build tinplating plant.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Gunung Sewu to build tinplating plant.

text.p: Indonesian conglomerate Gunung Sewu Group said on Monday the group and two local partners planned to form a joint venture with foreign firms to build a 150,000 tonne-per-year tinplating plant.

"We have received proposals for the joint venture from companies in Australia, Japan and South Korea. We are now selecting the right candidates and hope to reach a decision soon," Gunadi Stiawan, Gunung Sewu's associate director, told Reuters.
Gunadi declined to reveal the names of the foreign firms, but said the plant, to be located in Serang, West Java, was expected to cost $70 million.
Construction was expected to begin in early 1997 and commercial production to commence between the middle and the end of 1998, he said.
"We've got many proposals for the joint venture plan because they know we have a captive market for the tinplate," he said.
Most of the tin-plated steel sheet used for making cans would be sold to Gunung Sewu and two local partners, United Can and Ancol Perang, he said.
Both United and Ancol are among the country's largest can manufacturers. Gunung Sewu has interests in agribusiness, with extensive pineapple, casava and banana plantations, and finance and property.
Indonesia currently consumes some 240,000 tonnes of tinplate annually while producing only around 130,000 tonnes, he said.
